title: Rounds 615–620: response shortlist coverage and paired strength check
status: complete; damage-ranked response proposal remains experimental
question: Can the fixed-width four-response search matrix include the opponent's realized joint response more often without widening the matrix?

method.round615_618_619: 64 same-seed team-pair clusters per opponent; two hidden-world samples per decision; compare semantic and damage-ranked shortlist inclusion
method.round620: 256 fresh team-pair clusters per opponent; both seats; raw policy and one-turn equilibrium search paired on the same matches; 2,048 matches total
method.search: 4 own candidates × 4 response candidates × 4 chance samples × 2 hidden worlds; one decision per match
method.value_model: Round609 trained from Round600h self-play outcomes

coverage.generation_audit: When the actual move IDs were available in the sampled hidden world, exact target/action semantics were generated in about 98% of cases. A forced-targetless Solar Beam target normalization defect in the diagnostic was corrected; it did not alter battle or search behavior.

round620_score.interpretation: Neither comparison supports a strength gain. Coverage increased at the same matrix width, but the shortlist change has not improved paired full-match outcomes. Do not promote search or this response selector.

speed.decision_budget: 10 seconds; one search decision per match
speed.measurement_limit: These are workload-specific complete-match rates, not training rollout rates and not a controlled speed comparison with earlier rounds.
speed.bottleneck: For this search workload, Showdown branch advancement and candidate/chance evaluation dominate. For training rollout throughput, the current measured bottleneck remains CPU action selection/policy inference and observation encoding; the GPU learner is not the dominant rollout path.

decision: Keep Round600h PPO as the playing baseline. Preserve damage_ranked as an experimental selectable strategy because it improves measured response coverage without widening the matrix, but do not deploy it as a strength improvement. Next work should improve response proposal quality and value/action alignment, then validate on a new paired cohort; do not spend more time widening the matrix absent a powered strength gain.
